title: Share the British Fencing licence across everyone who tracks a fencer
body:
## Summary

The British Fencing licence is now a shared property of the fencer, not a private annotation on one account. Anyone who tracks the fencer may set or correct it; last write wins, with `setBy` / `setAt` provenance. Two parents tracking the same child both see British standings after either one types the number.

This reverses the original "do not promote one user's guess into a global fact" decision in `docs/design-docs/british-fencing-rankings-as-a-standings-source.md`. The scraper-ownership objection was **not** dismissed: the value lives in a new `fencer_british_licences` Cosmos collection (`fencer_licence` crate), keyed by fencer id (`bfl-{fencerViewId}`), which `SyncFencerInfo` / `merge_into` cannot address. `fencer_refresh_merge_does_not_patch_a_licence_path` pins that a fencer refresh emits no licence patch and that `FencerFields` JSON has no `britishFencingLicence` key.

Writes still go through `PUT /api/v3/user/tracked-fencers/{fencerId}/british-fencing-membership` (caller must track the fencer). `GET /api/v2/user/me` hydrates `trackedFencers[].britishFencingLicence` from the sidecar in a single batched query (`cosmos::id_in` over the tracked fencer ids) so the settings editor does not need a new read; a failure to load the sidecar degrades that field to unset rather than failing the whole `/user/me` response. That field is no longer a stored per-user assertion: the write path does not patch the user document, the generic `PATCH /api/v2/user/me` json-patch endpoint unconditionally rejects any path containing `britishFencingLicence`, and a one-shot migration strips leftover keys.

Standings / composition / history still require a **tracking viewing context** (signed-in caller who tracks the fencer, or a live results-share link whose owner tracks the bound fencer). A signed-out visitor with no share token still sees no British chips. Share links are not widened beyond that owner-scoped grant.

Capture no longer has a multi-asserter ambiguity path. One shared record cannot produce two values, so `resolve_british_licence` / `BritishLicenceResolution::Ambiguous` / `CaptureCounts.britishLicenceAmbiguous` are gone.

### Migration

Via admin task `migrate_british_fencing_licences` only — it is not run automatically on backend startup, since it does a full uncached scan of the users container and every replica would otherwise pay that cost on every process start:

- Exactly one distinct per-user licence for a fencer → adopt it (`setBy` = lexicographically-smallest asserting user id).
- Two or more distinct licences → leave the shared record unset, log a warning with **fencer id and distinct-count only** (never the membership ids), and leave that fencer's per-user `britishFencingLicence` values in place on the user documents so the competing assertions stay recoverable until a human reconciles them.
- A fencer that already has a sidecar record is not overwritten.
- Then strip `britishFencingLicence` from user documents that still carry it, except for fencers left in conflict above.

This workspace has no production user documents, so this run cannot report live bucket counts. Running the `migrate_british_fencing_licences` admin task in production/staging logs `adopted`, `conflicted`, `skipped_already_shared`, and `users_stripped`.

### Assumptions

- A sidecar collection is the way to keep a hand-typed value off scraper-owned `FencerFields` without requiring a fencer document to exist for every `f.u.*` tracked fencer.
- `TrackedFencer.britishFencingLicence` stays on the GET `/user/me` response as a hydrated field so the settings UI does not need a new endpoint. It is not a second write path.
- Share links resolve the **shared** licence after confirming the owner tracks the fencer. That is how a spouse-set licence appears on the owner's share page; the public fencer-id route still does not load the licence.

## Validation

- `bazel test --build_tests_only //backend/...` — pass, including new unit tests for the previously-untested blob-side migration and hydration orchestration (`collect_assertions`, `strip_licence_except`) and for the `britishFencingLicence` patch-path rejection
- `bazel build //backend:backend` — pass
- `./tools/checks run` — no findings
- `npm --prefix frontend run build` (`tsc && vite build`) — pass

## Open Questions

None. Production migration bucket counts will appear in the `migrate_british_fencing_licences` admin task log lines (`adopted`, `conflicted`, `skipped_already_shared`, `users_stripped`) when it is run.

[workspace]
members = [
  "backend",
  "backend/admintasks",
  "backend/blob",
  "backend/british_fencing",
  "backend/bout",
  "backend/cache",
  "backend/cosmos",
  "backend/cron_schedule",
  "backend/dates",
  "backend/event_notes",
  "backend/event_types",
  "backend/family",
  "backend/fencingtimelive",
  "backend/fencingtracker",
  "backend/fencingtracker_parse",
  "backend/field_strength_snapshot",
  "backend/flunge_config",
  "backend/google",
  "backend/http_helper",
  "backend/ids",
  "backend/invitations",
  "backend/json_redact",
  "backend/manual_tournaments",
  "backend/model_common",
  "backend/names",
  "backend/points_tables",
  "backend/predicate",
  "backend/qualification",
  "backend/ratings_policy",
  "backend/rec_contrib_low_level",
  "backend/rec_contrib_rating_field",
  "backend/rec_engine",
  "backend/rec_projected_impact",
  "backend/redis_backoff",
  "backend/retry_backoff",
  "backend/scrape",
  "backend/share_links",
  "backend/standings_history",
  "backend/standings_index",
  "backend/tasks",
  "backend/text_match",
  "backend/trial_tables",
  "backend/unified_snapshot",
  "backend/usafencing",
  "backend/requestz",
  "backend/routez",
  "backend/runtime_flags",
  "backend/util",
  "backend/view_ratings",
  "checks/cache-registry",
  "cli/logq",
  "cli/release_orchestrator",
]
resolver = "3"

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

[workspace.dependencies]
anyhow = { version = "1.0.96", features = ["backtrace"] }
arraydeque = "0.5.1"
assert_matches = "*"
async-trait = "0.1.86"
axum = { version = "0.8.4", features = ["macros"] }
axum-extra = { version = "0.10.1", features = ["cookie", "query"] }
azure-communications = "0.1.1"
azure_core = "0.20.0"
azure_data_cosmos = "0.20.0"
base64 = "0.22.1"
admintasks = { path = "backend/admintasks" }
blob = { path = "backend/blob" }
bon = "3.6.3"
bout = { path = "backend/bout" }
brotli = "8.0.2"
cached = { version = "0.56.0", features = [
  "async",
  "proc_macro",
  "redis",
  "redis_store",
  "redis_tokio",
] }
chrono = { version = "0.4.40", features = ["serde"] }
chrono-tz = "0.10.1"
clap = { version = "4.5.31", features = ["derive"] }
confique = { version = "0.3.0", features = ["toml"] }
cron = "0.15.0"
cron_schedule = { path = "backend/cron_schedule" }
csv = "1.3.1"
ctor = "0.5.0"
derivative = "2.2.0"
derive_builder = "0.20.2"
flunge_config = { path = "backend/flunge_config" }
event_notes = { path = "backend/event_notes" }
futures = "0.3.31"
globset = "0.4.18"
governor = "0.10.1"
http = "1.2.0"
itertools = "0.14.0"
json-patch = "4.0.0"
jsonwebtoken = "9.3.1"
lazy_static = "1.5.0"
levenshtein = "1.0.5"
map-macro = "0.3.0"
markup = "0.15.0"
metrics = "0.24.1"
metrics-exporter-prometheus = { version = "0.17.2", default-features = false, features = [
  "http-listener",
] }
nanoid = "0.4.0"
nonzero_ext = "0.3.0"
paste = "1.0.15"
pdf-extract = "0.9.0"
rand = "0.9.0"
redis = { version = "0.32.5", features = ["aio", "tokio-comp"] }
runtime_flags = { path = "backend/runtime_flags" }
regex = "1.11.1"
reqwest = { version = "0.12.12", default-features = false, features = [
  "json",
  "stream",
  "gzip",
  "brotli",
  "deflate",
  "cookies",
] }
rust-embed = { version = "8.6.0", features = ["debug-embed"] }
scraper = "0.24.0"
serde = { version = "1.0.218", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.139"
serde_qs = "0.15.0"
serde_with = "3.12.0"
serde_yaml = "0.9.34"
sha2 = "0.10.9"
strsim = "0.11.1"

before.content:
# Backend

The backend is a Rust binary in `backend/` using Axum as the web framework.

## Building

```sh
bazel build //backend:backend
```

To run it locally, the binary loads `config.toml`, `config-common.toml`, and `config-secrets.toml` by relative path from its cwd, and the `//backend:backend` target has no `data` deps for them, so run it from within `backend/` (where those files live) rather than via `bazel run`:

```sh
cd backend && ../bazel-bin/backend/backend
```

`config-secrets.toml` isn't checked in (see [`config-secrets.toml.gpg`](../backend/config-secrets.toml.gpg)); decrypt it first if it's missing from your checkout.

The backend serves at http://localhost:8080. Check http://localhost:8080/statusz for health.

## Workspace Structure

The backend is a Cargo workspace (edition 2024, resolver 3) with these member crates:

| Crate                  | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `admintasks`           | Scheduled and manually-triggered admin tasks (`push_results`, `rebuild_standings_index`, `migrate_bouts`, the connected-fencer backfills, `reconcile_inprogress_registrations`). Depends on `blob` for the DB/`TaskManager`/view vocabulary its tasks drive, so the `admintasks` → `blob` edge is one-directional and nothing in `blob` may import it: `backend/main.rs` registers the tasks and the two startup/admin hooks through `blob::startup::Extensions` (see [Internal refactor notes](backend/refactors.md#admintasks-extracted-out-of-blob-into-its-own-crate-2026-07-17)).                                                                                                                                                            |
| `blob`                 | Main application logic (routes, services, scrapers)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `bout`                 | Bout storage domain unit: `BoutFields`/`Video` models, deterministic bout ids, and the bout repository. Depends only on `cosmos` + `ids` + `model_common`. The repository takes a `cosmos::Collection<BoutFields>` as an argument, so `blob` keeps the `DbClient` wiring and the `blob` → `bout` edge stays one-directional (see [Results notes](backend/results.md#bout-storage-crate)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `cosmos`               | Azure Cosmos DB client                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `event_types`          | Addendum `EventType` vocabulary: the `TournamentType`/`NationalSubType` + fencer-category → `EventType` mapping, division-qualifier detection, slot identity, and the national rolling-points PDF detail-table vocabulary. Pure keyword/data mapping; depends only on `model_common` + `rec_engine` + `ratings_policy` + `util`. Consumed by both `blob::recommendations` and `blob::usafencing::standings` (see [Recommendations notes](backend/recommendations.md#v3-recommendation-engine-notes)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `flunge_config`        | Configuration loading                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `google`               | Google API integration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `http_helper`          | HTTP client utilities                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `ids`                  | ID generation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `invitations`          | Invitation domain unit: `InvitationFields`/`InvitationType`/`InvitationStatus` models, `InvitationError`, and the invitation repository. Depends only on `cosmos` + `ids` + `family`. The repository takes a `cosmos::Collection<InvitationFields>` as an argument, so `blob` keeps the `DbClient` wiring and the `blob` → `invitations` edge stays one-directional. The HTTP API, invitation emails, and scheduled tasks stay in `blob`, which re-exports the crate's surface as `crate::invitations`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `model_common`         | Shared data models                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `points_tables`        | USA Fencing points/ranking reference data and event classification: the verbatim Legacy point tables (§5.2 domestic, §4.2 ROC, §12.1 Veteran Age), field-size scoring cutoffs, the Addendum's `EventType`/`RankingCategory`/`RocDivision` vocabulary, and the points→rank projection over a standings curve. Pure reference data; depends only on `model_common` + `serde`. Extracted out of `rec_engine`'s `projected_impact` module so the tables rebuild/retest on their own; `rec_engine` re-exports its whole surface, so consumers see an unchanged API (see [Recommendations notes](backend/recommendations.md#v3-recommendation-engine-notes)).                                                                                           |
| `ratings_policy`       | USA Fencing national-event rating policy: the Ratings Chart criteria tables, guaranteed minimums, youth/cadet C1 floor, and tournament-type classification. The public `get_national_standings`/`refresh_national_standings_cache`/`get_region_standings`/`refresh_region_standings_cache` functions remain as thin wrappers with unchanged signatures — this is a pure internal refactor and the standings routes' request/response contracts are unchanged.

Fixed by removing the `skip` attribute so the field round-trips normally, and adding a `FencerStandingPublic` REST DTO (dropping just that one field) for the two routes above and `usafencing::api::rest`'s `/standings/national/{classifier}` and `/standings/region/{region_id}/{classifier}`, which previously serialized `FencerStanding` directly — since the field was never actually emitted before either (the `skip` stripped it from responses too), every route's JSON response shape is byte-for-byte unchanged. The cache key literals gained a `:v2` suffix (`view:standings:national:v2`/`view:standings:regional:v2`, the same "bump the namespace" convention `docs/backend/recommendations.md`'s `recommendations_compute_v2` rename uses) so entries written under the old key — permanently missing the field, with no TTL to expire them out on its own — are orphaned rather than served stale; `get_standings`'s existing on-miss `refresh_standings_cache` repopulates each region/classifier under the new key on its next read or `rebuild_standings_index` tick. See `docs/backend/recommendations.md`'s matching note for the paired sec-17 "known zero vs. unknown" refusal-semantics fix in the projected-impact contributor that consumes this cache.
- **The `:v2` view-cache bump above didn't bust the upstream scrape cache, so pre-fix rows could repopulate it (2026-07-15 follow-up).** `refresh_standings_cache` (used by both request-time misses and `rebuild_standings_index` ticks) rebuilds the view cache by calling straight through `usafencing::api::get_region_standings`, which is itself a `redis_cached!`-wrapped scrape cache (`usafencing_region_standings`, TTL 86400s) that the `:v2` rename above never touched. A rebuild tick that happened to read a pre-fix entry there (still live for up to a day after the fix shipped) would write its entry-id-less rows straight into the brand-new `view:standings:regional:v2` cache, reproducing the exact "fencer found in cached regional standings but missing entry id" refusal the `:v2` bump was meant to close — confirmed live against a region-3 Y12MS evaluation. Fixed two ways: (1) the upstream cache name itself gained the same `:v2`-style bump (`usafencing_region_standings_v2` in `backend/blob/src/usafencing/api.rs`, `config-common.toml`), orphaning any pre-fix scrape entry the same way the view-cache rename did; and (2) `refresh_standings_cache` now refuses to write a regional standings list into the view cache when every row has `regional_entry_id: None` (`is_poisoned_regional_standings`) — that state is only producible by the old bug and is worthless to the recommendations path — logging loudly and returning the (unwritten) list instead, so a future stale-cache reintroduction degrades to "keep re-fetching" rather than "poison the view cache again." National standings are exempt from that guard since `regional_entry_id: None` on every row is their normal, correct shape.
- **A points-floor Unified composition permanently deleted the standing from the connected-fencer list (fixed 2026-08-09).** `get_standing_composition_handler` persists each composition's verdict at `view:standings:composition-verdict:v1`, keyed by `(fencer id, standing key, published points)`; the hash has no TTL, and the key only changes when the published points do. `standings_for_view` then drops any summary whose cached verdict says its total did not reconcile, on the reasoning that such a row's displayed total is not supported by source evidence. That reasoning holds only for an _earned_ total. A points-floor row's total is derived from a weapon rating rather than from results, so no counted set can ever sum to it and its composition **always** refuses with `didNotReconcile` — the deliberate, documented behaviour of the snapshot-side reconcile gate. Honouring that structural refusal as negative evidence meant the first person to open a floored Unified card's breakdown permanently deleted that card from `GET /api/v3/view/standings/fencer/{id}`. Observed live on `f.u.100344621`, whose Senior Men's Saber Unified standing (rank 1134, 50.0 points, `E26` floor) vanished seconds after its composition was requested at 2026-08-09 06:50:03Z, in both staging and production. `total_is_rating_derived` in `view/standings/fencer.rs` now exempts floored rows on **both** sides: `retain_substantiated` never suppresses one (so verdicts already persisted by earlier builds heal without a cache-key bump), and `should_record_did_not_reconcile` writes `false` rather than skipping the write (so a row that stops being floored overwrites its old verdict instead of inheriting it). The exemption is scoped to floored rows — an earned Unified total that fails to reconcile is still genuine negative evidence and is still suppressed. Floored-ness on the snapshot is the presence of `pointsFloor` itself (`is_floored_row` alone), not whether the weapon-rating string parsed: `PointsFloor.weaponRating` may be null when the source string is unparseable, but the row is still treated as rating-derived.

## Unified standings list endpoint

- `GET /api/v3/view/standings/unified/{classifier}` serves the active atomic Unified catalog snapshot. Classifiers are parsed through the normal canonicalizer, so USA Fencing's `SNR...` aliases resolve to Flunge's canonical `STM...` classifier codes.
- The route's snapshot loader is also the refresh task's post-publication acceptance boundary. This prevents the task from reporting success when storage publication returned `Ok` but the public read path would still return 503, address an older snapshot, expose an empty list, or project fewer rows than USA Fencing declared.
- Unlike National and Regional lists, the response is an envelope: `scope: "unified"`, canonical classifier information, public standings rows, `isNew`, `source` metadata (`listCode`, `seasonId`, `seasonLabel`, `sourceUpdatedAt`, `fetchedAt`, `isStale`), an envelope-level `eligibility` (below), and `identity` (next bullet). Timestamps are Unix seconds. Source-specific row handles and internal regional entry ids are never exposed.
- `identity` is `{ "resolvedRows", "totalRows", "complete" }` — how much of this list Flunge has bound to a Flunge membership. Publishing does not wait for identity resolution (see the refresh notes above), so a list can legitimately serve while memberships are still being resolved and `complete` is `false`. Clients must not render a row with `id: null` as "not a tracked fencer" when `complete` is `false`: that states a conclusion nobody reached. The distinction is the same one the backend keeps between a `pending` row (nobody has looked yet) and an `unresolved` one (FencingTracker answered and nothing matched).
- `isStale` is calculated from the last successful snapshot's `fetchedAt` (more than 36 hours old). Failed refreshes retain the active last-known-good snapshot and its source metadata, allowing callers to display that warning while continuing to show standings.
- If no snapshot has been published, the endpoint returns HTTP 503 rather than an empty list. `isNew` is server-controlled by the `standings.unified_new_marker_enabled` runtime flag, enabled by default.
- Each standing row is additive to the usual public shape: it adds `pointsFloor` and a per-row `eligibility`, both new fields (`FencerStandingPublic`, and the National/Regional routes' response shape, are unchanged).
  - `pointsFloor` is `null` for a row whose points were earned from `counted` results. It is `{ "weaponRating": { "category": "C", "year": 2026, "weapon": null } | null }` for a row USA Fencing floors at a minimum tied to a fencer's weapon rating as of August 1 — the source sends these with either an empty `results` array or a partial one that falls short of the floor, and non-zero `points` (see `usafencing::unified::UnifiedStanding::weapon_rating`/`ties` and `unified_catalog::is_floored_row`, the single shared check `validate_catalog_list` and this derivation both read from, so they can never disagree on which rows are floored). `weaponRating` is a `model_common::FencerRating` (the same rating shape used elsewhere in the API — never a raw source string) when the source classification parses; it is `null` only in the defensive unparseable-string case (`parse_floor_rating`), which does not undo floored-ness — presence of `pointsFloor` alone is the floored signal. The floor's numeric value is not duplicated here — it is already the row's own `points`, computed by USA Fencing; Flunge never reproduces USA Fencing's year/letter floor table, instead checking published-value membership via `usafencing::unified::points_floor::is_recognized_floor_points`. A row whose rating is unrated (`"U"`) or whose points match no recognized floor value is not reported as floored — an unrated fencer has no floor under the published policy, and an unrecognized value is not a legitimate floor.
  - The envelope-level `eligibility` is `{ "category": "CDT"|"JNR"|"DVI", "minimumPoints" }` — the national-event category and minimum this list's classifier gates, constant across every row and so serialized once rather than duplicated onto every one of a list's (potentially thousands of) rows. It is absent when the list's classifier has no national-event category, or its season has no configured minimums (see below).
  - Each row's `eligibility` is `{ "eligible", "margin" }`: whether this fencer's current `points` (floored or earned — the same number) meets the envelope's `minimumPoints`, and by how much. `margin` is `points - minimumPoints`, negative when short. A row's `eligibility` is absent exactly when the envelope's `eligibility` is absent.
  - These minimums (`points_tables::national_event_eligibility`) have no source endpoint — USA Fencing's feed exposes no eligibility flag anywhere in the probed payload — so they are recorded as reference data (150/100/100 for DVI/JNR/CDT, "Events Restructure | Important Registration Updates", USA Fencing, 2026-08-05) rather than derived, keyed by the season they apply to (`model_common::Season`, resolved from the list's own `seasonId` — never the current calendar date, so a past snapshot is never re-evaluated against a later season's revised minimums), and re-evaluated on every read rather than cached. A season with no configured minimums yields no `eligibility` rather than a guessed value. This lives in `points_tables` — the repo's USA Fencing reference-data leaf — rather than in `usafencing` (parsing/scraping only).
- `GET /api/v3/view/standings/fencer/{fencer_id}` (below) mirrors both fields per Unified item — `pointsFloor` and a single-row `eligibility` shaped `{ "category", "minimumPoints", "eligible", "margin" }` (no envelope to hoist the constant pair into, since it's one row).

## Connected-fencer standings endpoint

- `GET /api/v3/view/standings/fencer/{fencer_id}` returns the current standings for a single connected fencer, enriched with points and entrant counts. Public (optional auth), consistent with the existing standings/results endpoints.
- Path param `fencer_id` is in view format (`f.u.{usafId}` or `f.d.{dbId}`). A `f.d.*` fencer without a linked USAF id yields HTTP 200 with `"identityResolved": false`; its `standings` can still contain British items when the caller supplies a matching British Fencing licence through an owner-scoped context. Malformed ids yield 400.
- Response shape: `{ "fencerId": "f.u.12345", "standings": [{ "key": "s.d.nat-SNRMF"|"s.d.r3-JNRME"|"s.d.rs-D1AWS"|"s.d.uni-CDTWS"|"s.d.gb-CDTWS", "scope": "national"|"regional"|"unified"|"british", "regionId": null|1..6, "classifier": { "weapon", "gender", "category", "code", "label" }, "rank": { "position", "isTied" }, "points"?, "entrants"?, "sourceUpdatedAt"?, "fetchedAt"?, "isStale"?, "isNew"?, "pointsFloor"?, "eligibility"? }] }`. `sourceUpdatedAt`/`fetchedAt`/`isStale` are a shared, source-agnostic `SourceFreshness` block (`backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs`) present on both Unified and British items; `isNew`, `pointsFloor`, and `eligibility` remain Unified-only. `pointsFloor` and `eligibility` follow the same shapes and absence rules documented above for the Unified list endpoint's per-row fields (`eligibility` here is the single-row `{ "category", "minimumPoints", "eligible", "margin" }` shape, since a per-fencer tile has no list envelope to hoist the constant pair into).
- `regionId` is `null` for national standings AND for Division categories (Division I-A, Division II) whose regional ranking is a single combined list across all regions — not per-region — AND for every British item (British Fencing publishes no regional dimension). `regionId` is `1..6` only for categories that genuinely have per-region lists (Youth, Cadet, Junior).
- `key` is a typed standing ID: `s.d.{opaqueId}`. The `s` entity marker identifies a standing and `d` identifies this Flunge-derived record as database-owned; the opaque ID is `nat-{code}` for national standings, `r{regionId}-{code}` for genuine per-region standings, `rs-{code}` for the Division combined-regional standings that carry no `regionId`, `uni-{code}` for Unified standings, and `gb-{code}` for British Fencing standings. `{code}` is the classifier's code field (e.g. `SNRMF`, `D1AWS`, `CDTWS`). Built by `build_standing_key` in `backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs` and parsed through the shared `view::ids::parse_typed_id` mechanism.

### British Fencing standings items

- British Fencing's published live-ranking tables are a fourth `scope` on this same per-fencer response, reusing the existing item shape, chip, and (for now) leaving the breakdown modal's per-source coverage unchanged -- see [the design doc](../design-docs/british-fencing-rankings-as-a-standings-source.md) for the full source contract and rationale. Assembly is enabled by default; `standings.british_rankings_enabled` remains an operational kill switch for disabling serving if the upstream source breaks. Ingestion (`admintasks::refresh_british_rankings`, daily at 06:00 UTC) runs regardless.
- A British item is keyed by a **British Fencing licence**, not a USA Fencing membership number, and never enters `standings:index` -- it is looked up separately from the per-table licence index (`standings:british:v1:licence-index`) and the last-published, validated per-table payload (`standings:british:v1:table:{tableId}`), both owned by the `british_fencing::store` module so the writer (`admintasks`) and the reader (`blob`) share one key layout. `points` is the source's published integer total; `entrants` is the parsed row count of that table (never the table's highest rank, which is denser than the row count on a tied field).
- **The endpoint cannot resolve a licence from the fencer id alone** -- unlike a USAF id, the licence lives on a signed-in user's own `TrackedFencer` record, not on the shared fencer document (see the design doc's "Where the membership id lives"). `GET /api/v3/view/standings/fencer/{fencer_id}` therefore layers `optional_auth_middleware` (`crate::auth`, shared with `/registrations/*/field-strength`) onto just that route: a signed-in caller's own tracked-fencer record for this exact fencer id supplies the licence; a signed-out caller (or one who tracks the fencer with no licence configured) sees every other scope unchanged and simply no British item.
- **The anonymous results-share surface gets the same data without sign-in.** `GET /api/v3/share/results/view/standings` (`backend/blob/src/share/view.rs`) resolves the live bearer link (`X-Flunge-Share-Token`), then that link's own `owner_user_id`'s tracked-fencer record for the link's bound `fencer_id` -- never the recipient's own session, if any, which this route never reads. It reuses the exact same internal assembly (`view::standings::fencer::get_fencer_standings`) the owner route uses, then the same `standings_view_payload` (`attach_movement` then `standings_for_view`) so shared tiles get the owner's movement indicator for every scope the link already renders. A missing or unparseable movement hash omits the block and does not fail the share render. It inherits the share surface's generic-404, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, 30-req/min rate limit, and one-fencer-per-link guarantees the same way every other `crate::share::view` route does. `GET /api/v3/share/results/view/standings/{standingKey}/composition` mirrors the owner composition route below the same way, resolving the link's own owner-scoped licence rather than any caller-supplied one. There is no share-token history route.
- **Not-yet-ranked is silent.** A licence that matches no row on a configured table produces no item for that table -- no error, no placeholder -- and `identityResolved` is untouched: it means "this fencer id could not be resolved to a USA Fencing identity" and stays exactly that, regardless of whether a British licence is configured or matched. The _Web: British standings chip_ entry must relax `FencerStandingsCallout`'s `identityResolved === false` short-circuit so it renders these licence-matched British items before falling back to the unresolved state.
- `GET /api/v3/view/standings/fencer/{fencer_id}/composition/{standing_key}` resolves one of those server-minted keys for the fencer. It echoes the standing identity (`fencerId`, `standingKey`, `scope`, `regionId`, `classifier`, and `points`) and uses a top-level `availability` discriminator for the body. Malformed standing keys return 400 and keys not held by the fencer return 404.

- `GET /api/v3/view/standings/fencer/{fencer_id}/history/{standing_key}?days=N` returns one standing's captured trajectory. `days` defaults to 180 and is capped at the configured history retention; malformed keys return 400 and a current-standing mismatch returns 404, matching the composition route. Its `points` contain projected observations (`runId`, `capturedAt`, rank, points, entrants, source staleness, and composition capture state/reason) without the stored contributor arrays. `gaps` explicitly enumerates scheduled Monday/Thursday slots where capture failed, no capture was attempted, or the successful capture observed that the fencer no longer held the standing. The top-level optional `movement` is the same precomputed summary carried by a current standings item.
  - **National Cadet/Junior/Senior** (`scope: "national"`, `classifier.category` one of `cadet`/`junior`/`senior`) uses the per-member composition index `view::standings::write_national_composition` persists at ingest (`view:standings:composition:v1:{classifier}`, keyed by USA Fencing member id). Its stored `AggregationPolicy::GroupSplit` window produces source `nationalDetailPdf` and rule code `groupSplit`.
  - **National Youth** (Y10/Y12/Y14) fetches the fencer's live USA Fencing points-page breakdown through `usafencing::api::get_national_fencer_breakdown`. It uses `AggregationPolicy::YouthBestFour(youth_caps(..))` and national slot-reoccurrence, producing source `nationalPointsPage` and rule code `youthBestFour`; it is not interchangeable with the national detail-PDF source. Y10/Y12/Y14 is the whole of that endpoint's coverage: `points/national/{g}{w}/{cat}/{member_id}` is the CSV whole-list path plus a member segment, so `usafencing::standings::national_list_has_fencer_breakdown` (the same `uses_national_csv` authority the whole-list scrape uses) is what every caller must consult first — a Cadet/Junior/Senior/Veteran per-fencer URL has never existed and 404s unconditionally. A 404 on a list the endpoint _does_ serve means the fencer holds no rows on it, and is modelled as `NationalFencerBreakdown::FencerNotRanked` (→ `notInSourceList` here), not as an error; only a transport failure, a non-404 status, or a parse failure is still an `Err` (→ `upstreamUnavailable`).
  - **Regional standings** reuse `rec_projected_impact::fetch_regional_contributions`, including its cached-list `regional_entry_id` resolution, then apply the configured regional season and `AggregationPolicy::BestN`. Successful responses use source `regionalPointsPage` and rule code `bestN`. This dependency is why a missing `regional_entry_id` is an `upstreamUnavailable` signal instead of a fabricated empty breakdown. Combined regional Division lists (`regionId: null`) have no per-region source and still refuse with `listNotSupported`.
  - **Unified Cadet/Junior/Senior** standings serve the counted set straight from the active atomic Unified list snapshot, which already stores every result USA Fencing marked as carried for the member's row. No upstream request is needed to answer "what makes up this total": `unified_catalog::validate_catalog_list` refuses to publish a non-floor row whose per-row carried scores do not sum to that row's published points, so the stored set reconciles by construction. Successful responses use source `unifiedRankings` and rule code `bestN`; `rule.best` is the active list's validated `maxResults`, not a duplicated constant. The source's `counted` boolean alone determines the counted set. Every result is strictly mapped from its event code, date, placement, ranking score, and tournament classification before the response is complete; an unknown or unmappable source event refuses with `resultMappingUnavailable` rather than silently dropping it or misreporting a local coverage gap as an upstream outage. Division IA, II, and III result codes map to the shared `senior` composition category, matching USA Fencing's Unified category model. The counted `rankingScore` sum must reconcile with the active Unified standing within `DETAIL_RECONCILE_TOLERANCE` (1.0), or the response is `didNotReconcile` — which is what a points-floor row gets, since its points come from a weapon rating rather than from results and no counted list can explain the total.
    - The snapshot-side reconcile gate has narrower meaning than the other composition gates. It is no longer an independent cross-check between two source views: for every non-floor row it repeats the invariant already enforced when `validate_catalog_list` published the same snapshot. Its remaining serving-time effect is to refuse points-floor rows, which catalog validation deliberately admits and marks because their published total is rating-derived. The gate remains explicit so a complete body can never be emitted without checking the exact row it serves, but it must not be cited as independent source corroboration.
    - The source's _excluded_ set is the one thing the snapshot does not carry: it exists only behind `GET /rankings/{source_ranking_id}/results`, and USA Fencing re-mints that `ranking.id` handle on every ranking recompute — many times a day, against a catalog refreshed daily — so a stored handle is usually already dead (HTTP 404). That fetch is therefore a **best-effort enrichment**, made through the snapshot-keyed, 24-hour result cache and the shared request budget: when it succeeds the response carries the full counted-plus-excluded set, and when it fails (or its result set cannot be mapped or reconciled) the counted breakdown is still returned. A failed enrichment is never a refusal.
    - `excludedAvailability` (`complete` | `unavailable`) says which of those two happened. It is `complete` for every non-Unified source, whose exclusions are derived from the same candidate pool that produced the counted set. Clients must not read an empty `excluded` alone as "the source published no exclusions" — with `excludedAvailability: "unavailable"` it means "not retrieved", and both the web modal and the iOS sheet say so in copy.
    - Unified adds `retrievedAt` (Unix seconds) to a complete response _when the enrichment succeeded_; it is absent from a snapshot-only response, because nothing was retrieved on that request. `asOf` is the active list's maximum upstream result-update timestamp, while `retrievedAt` is when Flunge successfully fetched the complete per-fencer result set; clients must describe these as source-update and fetch provenance, not an official ranking publication time.
    - A source result marked `counted: false` is returned in `excluded` with `excludedReason: "sourceDidNotCount"`. Flunge deliberately does not infer `displacedByBestN`, because USA Fencing does not publish the reason for a false flag.
  - **British** (`scope: "british"`, `gb-{code}` key) serves the per-competition domestic/international breakdown from the stored table payload behind the owner-scoped licence (above), gated by the same reconcile-or-refuse tolerance as every other source. It uses source `britishFencingLiveRanking` and rule code `domesticInternationalSplit` (`{ "label", "domesticCounted", "internationalCounted" }`, both drawn from the table's own published per-bucket counted-event counts). `asOf` is the table's `sourceUpdatedAt`; there is no `retrievedAt` -- the whole table is already resident, nothing is fetched on demand. `excludedAvailability` is always `complete`. Each entry carries a `bucket` (`"domestic"`|`"international"`) reflecting British Fencing's own per-event classification, and the response carries `countedSelectionAmbiguous` -- British Fencing publishes only the counted totals per bucket, not which equal-scoring result won a bucket boundary tie, so a British entry omits `eventType`, `category`, and `sourceEventId` entirely (these are USA Fencing-only fields) and `group` is `null`.
  - Each source uses the same reconcile-or-refuse contract: it only returns `{ "availability": "complete", "source", "asOf", "retrievedAt"?, "rule", "countedTotal", "counted": [...], "excluded": [...], "countedSelectionAmbiguous"?, "excludedAvailability" }` when the counted total matches the card's `points` within `usafencing::standings::DETAIL_RECONCILE_TOLERANCE` (1.0). Entries are `{ "eventName", "eventType"?, "category"?, "group", "bucket"?, "date", "placing", "points", "excludedReason"? }`; `eventType` and `category` are present only for USA Fencing sources (National/Regional/Unified) and are omitted entirely for a British entry, which instead carries `bucket` (`"domestic"`|`"international"`); `group` is `null` for Youth, regional, Unified, and British results, and `excludedReason` is one of `displacedByBestN | cappedOutSyc | cappedOutNationalPerAge | outsideGroupWindow | rolledOffBySlotReoccurrence | priorSeason | sourceDidNotCount`. A mismatch returns `didNotReconcile` and logs both totals rather than exposing a misleading partial list.
  - A cached `didNotReconcile` verdict removes the standing from the list endpoint. A points-floor row is exempt on both sides of that cache (`total_is_rating_derived` in `view/standings/fencer.rs`): its total is rating-derived so its composition always refuses, which is not evidence against the standing; an earned Unified total that fails to reconcile is still suppressed.
  - National Veteran and Division IA/II (plus other national categories without one of these three sources) intentionally return `{ "availability": "unavailable", "reason": "listNotSupported" }`. `notInSourceList` means the fencer cannot be matched to the source list; `upstreamUnavailable` means a live fetch, cache read, regional entry-id lookup, or required points value is unavailable; `resultMappingUnavailable` means Flunge could not map every published result into its local composition vocabulary. These are distinct real refusals and are never converted to success.
- Unified items read points, entrant count, and source freshness from the active atomic Unified snapshot. `sourceUpdatedAt` and `fetchedAt` are Unix seconds; `isStale` is true once the snapshot is more than 36 hours old. `isNew` comes from the server-owned `standings.unified_new_marker_enabled` runtime flag (default true). Turning the flag off changes only that explicit field to `false`; it never removes Unified standings or their route.
- Results are ordered by scope first, then category within each scope: Unified, National, Regional, British (`scope_priority` in `backend/blob/src/view/standings/fencer.rs`). Every row of a higher-priority scope precedes every row of a lower one, regardless of category; `standings_sort_scope_first_then_orders_categories_within_scope` pins the actual behaviour.
- `points` and `entrants` are optional: if a legacy cached category list is absent at read time, rank is returned without them rather than failing. No new cache is introduced; reads reuse the existing Redis structures (`standings:index`, `view:standings:*`, and the active Unified snapshot) refreshed by `rebuild_standings_index` and the Unified catalog refresh.
- Implementation: `backend/blob/src/view/standings.rs` (`get_fencer_standings`, registered via `rest::router()`).
